description: canonical_bytes(subject) for subject.text/1 (verifier-toolkit/1 §8.5 + subject.text/1 §11): operate on the RAW input bytes (the subject context is opaque bytes per CCCP/1 §6.2; CCCP/1 §5.1 UTF-8/BOM rules do NOT apply here). Step 1 (§11.2): normalize line endings to CRLF in a single left-to-right pass over the original bytes — CRLF takes precedence, then lone CR -> CRLF, then lone LF -> CRLF. Step 2 (§11.3): strip the maximal trailing run of CRLF, then append exactly one CRLF. Everything else is byte-preserved: no UTF-8 validation, no Unicode normalization, no BOM stripping, embedded NUL preserved. subject_local_digest_hex = SHA3-256(canonical_bytes). These vectors pin the bytes so any toolkit in any language converges.
canonicalization: §11.2 line-ending normalization (single pass, CRLF longest-match) then §11.3 trailing-CRLF collapse to exactly one CRLF; all other bytes preserved exactly
digest: subject_local_digest_hex = SHA3-256(canonical_bytes), 32 bytes lowercase hex; verifier-local, never published
byte_notation: input_hex and canonical_hex are space-free lowercase hex of the raw byte sequence

vectors.name: 'a' + LF LF -> 'a' + one CRLF (trailing run collapses)
CR CR -> one CRLF (both are trailing)
CR CRLF (0d 0d 0a): §11.2 precedence -> lone CR then CRLF = two breaks -> one CRLF
LF CR (0a 0d): two line breaks, not one -> one CRLF
'a' CRLF 'b' -> internal CRLF kept, trailing CRLF appended

must_hold: line-ending normalization is a single left-to-right pass over the ORIGINAL bytes; CRLF matches before lone CR / lone LF
exactly one trailing CRLF in the output; an empty or all-CRLF input canonicalizes to exactly one CRLF
no UTF-8 validation, no Unicode normalization (NFC/NFD), no BOM stripping, no whitespace trimming, embedded NUL preserved
subject_local_digest_hex = SHA3-256(canonical_bytes), verifier-local, never published in a certificate
